meta.title: Open Pile Plan Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Pile Plan Studio: free, open-source engineering tool for pile plans. Review pile options per load point, select CPTs, compare utilization and cost, and optimize the plan. In the browser and for Windows, macOS and Linux.

header.label: Public alpha · Civil and geotechnical engineering
header.title: Open Pile Plan Studio
header.tagline: From loads and CPTs to a traceable pile plan
header.desc: Open-source engineering tool for pile plans. Bring load points, CPTs, foundation advice, pile options, utilization and estimated costs together in one interactive pile plan.

alt.plan: The pile plan of the sample project, with groups of load points and, on the right, the pile options for the selection

notice.text: Public alpha: the results are decision support. Always have input, assumptions and results checked by a qualified professional.

what.label: Workflow
what.title: What is Open Pile Plan Studio?
what.desc: An open-source engineering tool for reviewing pile options and assembling practical pile-plan variants. Structural loads, CPTs and available configurations come together in the browser and in the desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux, with the same Rust calculation core.

step1.title: 1. Combine sources
step1.desc: Import load points, CPTs and foundation advice and check their role.

step2.title: 2. Assess options
step2.desc: Inspect the plan view, the CPT selection, bearing capacity, utilization and cost.

step3.title: 3. Record choices
step3.desc: Assign configurations, review the whole plan and save everything as an IFCPP project.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From CPT to pile choice
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

options.title: See which piles work at every load point
options.desc: Select one or more locations and review every pile option with size, tip level, status, utilization, cost and the governing load point. Compression and optional tension are checked separately. Assign a configuration to one location or to a whole selection at once.

import.title: Three sources, one project
import.desc: Import load points, CPTs and foundation advice from CSV or Excel and give each file its role before import. A preview shows how the columns are read. CPTs are selected per quadrant or within a maximum angle, and you can adjust that choice by hand for each location.

optimize.title: The cheapest variant within your limits
optimize.desc: The HiGHS optimization looks for the lowest cost within the limits you set for tip levels, sizes and the number of configurations. It can then reduce differences between neighbours within an extra cost budget. The result reports whether the optimum was proven.

project.title: Variants side by side, everything in one file
project.desc: Work with several pile-plan variants in one project, share configurations within groups and lock choices. Explore a different number of piles per pile cap with proposals from 1 to 20 piles. Save everything as an IFCPP file, with undo and redo.

import.title: Purposeful project import
import.desc: Load points, CPTs and foundation advice from CSV or XLSX, with the role of each file chosen beforehand. Exports from an external structural analysis package are recognised.

advice.title: Foundation advice in any shape
advice.desc: One table row per value or an Excel matrix with one column per pile size, with a preview that shows how the file is read.

refresh.title: Refresh sources
refresh.desc: Read in new loads, CPTs or advice values and keep existing assignments and CPT selections where they still fit.

pileImport.title: Import an existing pile plan
pileImport.desc: Update a project from an Excel or CSV table, with checks on IDs and coordinates and a preview before import.

selection.title: Select CPTs
selection.desc: Automatically per quadrant or within a maximum angle, and overridable by hand for individual locations.

options.title: Compare pile options
options.desc: Valid, insufficient and missing options per location, with size, tip level and governing CPT.

tension.title: Compression and tension
tension.desc: Design loads in compression and, optionally, in tension are checked separately and both count when assigning and optimizing.

compare.title: Utilization and cost
compare.desc: Compare utilization, governing CPT and estimated cost before you record a configuration.

assign.title: Assign one or many
assign.desc: A configuration for one location or for a whole selection with common options.

interact.title: Interactive selection
interact.desc: Select by click, multi-selection or lasso and filter by pile size and tip level in the legend.

optimize.title: Minimize cost
optimize.desc: HiGHS finds the lowest cost within limits for tip levels, sizes and the number of configurations.

coherence.title: Fewer differences between neighbours
coherence.desc: Reduce differences in tip level and size between neighbouring locations within an extra cost budget, 5% by default.

quick.title: Quick improve
quick.desc: A fast local improvement method as an alternative to the full optimization.

caps.title: Pile cap proposals
caps.desc: Explore a different number of piles per pile cap, from 1 to 20, with indicative options and costs. The proposals are kept in the project.

groups.title: Groups and locks
groups.desc: Let locations in a group share the same configuration and lock assignments per plan.

variants.title: Pile-plan variants
variants.desc: Several named variants in one project, to compare plans side by side.

project.title: IFCPP project file
project.desc: Imported data, settings, pile choices and manual CPT selections together in one file, with undo, redo and recovery in the browser.

export.title: Export to Excel and CSV
export.desc: Pile assignments, proposed pile positions and CPTs to Excel or CSV, for reporting and coordination.

webdesktop.title: Browser and desktop
webdesktop.desc: The same Rust calculation core runs through WebAssembly in the browser and natively in the desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux.

mcp.title: MCP access for AI assistants
mcp.desc: The Windows app gives a local AI assistant access to the open project. Reading and editing are switched on separately.

sample.title: Explore right away
sample.desc: The browser demo opens with a complete sample project, so you can look at the workflow without any preparation.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v2026.46.0
download.lead: Free and without an account. Signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.metaMac: .dmg for Apple silicon and Intel, macOS 15 or later
download.mobileNote: Open Pile Plan Studio is made for a large screen. Open it on your computer, or take a look at the browser demo.
download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? Open Pile Plan Studio also runs in the browser, with the same calculation model. The connection with an AI assistant only works in the Windows app.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.46.0
whatsnew.title: A refreshed interface and its own logo
whatsnew.desc: Released on 9 November 2026. The interface now uses the shared components of the OpenAEC Blueprint, with the same controls and themes in the browser and on the desktop. The calculations and the IFCPP format are unchanged.

ui.title: Shared controls
ui.desc: Settings, inspection, optimization, import and export, the ribbon and the File menu now use the same buttons and fields as the other OpenAEC apps.

logo.title: Its own app logo
logo.desc: A white pile cap with three amber piles, in the title bar, the installers and the app icons.

theme.title: Light or dark plan view
theme.desc: The workspace follows the theme or gets its own background, with more legible CPT labels.

recent.title: Recent projects
recent.desc: The desktop app reopens recent IFCPP files; the browser keeps up to ten local copies.

feedback.title: Feedback without an account
feedback.desc: Send feedback through Open Feedback Studio, without a GitHub account and with images if you like.

speed.title: Smoother on the desktop
speed.desc: Calculations run outside the interface, and stopping or cancelling an optimization always works.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Pile Plan Studio is open source under the LGPL-3.0: no licence fees, no subscription and no account.

alpha.q: Can I use the results directly?
alpha.a: No. The app is a public alpha and supports engineering decisions, but it does not take over responsibility for the foundation design. The CPT selection is a practical approximation. Always have input, assumptions and results checked by a qualified professional.

data.a: Three tables in CSV or XLSX: load points (ID, X, Y and the design load), CPTs (ID, X and Y) and foundation advice (CPT, pile tip level, pile size and bearing capacity). Levels in metres, sizes in millimetres and forces in kN. The browser demo includes a sample project to get started.

web.q: What is the difference between the browser and the desktop app?
web.a: Both calculate with the same Rust core. The desktop apps are linked to IFCPP files and reopen recent projects; the Windows app also has the connection with an AI assistant. In the browser you save projects as a download and the app keeps up to ten local copies.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows x64, macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon and Intel, Linux x64 as .deb or AppImage (tested on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04), and any modern browser.

optimize.a: First the HiGHS solver looks for the lowest cost within your limits for tip levels, sizes and the number of configurations. It can then reduce the differences between neighbouring locations within an extra cost budget, 5% by default. The result states whether the optimum was proven. Quick improve is a faster, local method.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The Windows app has MCP access. Switch the connection on in the settings, and a local assistant can read the open project, compare plans and start the optimization. Changes are only possible once you separately allow editing; every change goes through the same checks as in the app.

signed.a: Yes. The Windows installer is digitally signed, the Mac version is signed and notarized by Apple, and the Linux packages have a detached OpenPGP signature. With the SHA256SUMS file you can verify all four installers.

why.title: Why Open Pile Plan Studio?
why.desc: A pile plan is often manual work, spread across spreadsheets, foundation advice reports and drawings. Open Pile Plan Studio brings that information together in one workspace, so you see right away which configurations work and record your choices traceably. Free and open source, for structural engineers, geotechnical consultants and foundation specialists.
